bounded_statement: Within the visible files, each authorized source item (a distinct ordered k1,k2 pair) contributes two measurements (columns a and b of its single row) that are placed into the two samples of mannwhitneyu, a procedure whose validity assumes the two samples consist of mutually independent observations; thus each of the 12 source items enters the independence-assuming procedure twice, with the report confirming a 12-vs-12 independent-samples comparison.

counterevidence_considered.description: All 12 ordered (k1,k2) pairs are distinct across the staged rows, so there is no row-level duplication of a source item; under a reading where one 'entry' equals one staged row, each unit enters only once.

evidence.description: The task authorizes the ordered (k1,k2) pair as the single source item.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. Treat each distinct ordered `k1`,`k2` pair as one source item; rows carrying the same ordered pair originate from the same source item.

evidence.description: Each source item's row carries two measurements, a and b, which the workflow routes into the two samples of mannwhitneyu, an independent-samples rank test.

source_refs.quoted_text:
left = [float(row["a"]) for row in rows]
right = [float(row["b"]) for row in rows]
result = mannwhitneyu(left, right)

evidence.description: The reported U statistic of 60.5 with a p-value from the standard two-sample distribution is consistent with a 12-vs-12 comparison in which all 24 observations from the 12 source items were ranked as independent.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted the alternative reading that 'entry' is row-level, under which the 12 distinct pairs each enter once and no issue exists. I rejected it because mannwhitneyu jointly ranks the 24 scalar observations under an assumption that the two samples are independent; each authorized source item contributes one observation to each sample, so the same unit enters the procedure twice and the assumed independence between its two entries is contradicted by the task's own unit definition. I also verified no deduplication or pairing-aware alternative (e.g., a signed-rank test) was used in the code. Residual uncertainty is interpretive (granularity of 'entry'), not evidential.

root_cause: The workflow splits the within-item paired measurements a and b of every row across the two samples of an independent-samples Mann-Whitney U test instead of using a procedure that accounts for within-item dependence, so each task-defined source item is entered twice into a procedure whose validity assumes each observation comes from an independent unit.
